goal: List the main risks of splitting a monolith into microservices, and how to mitigate each one.

children.title: Identify and mitigate main risks
children.instructions: Identify the 8 main risks of splitting a monolith into microservices (for example: distributed system complexity, data consistency and splitting the database, wrong service boundaries, network latency and partial failures, testing and debugging difficulty, operational/observability overhead, organisational and skills mismatch, migration cost and stalled migrations, security surface area). For each risk give: a one-sentence description of what goes wrong, and 2-4 concrete mitigations (named patterns or practices such as strangler fig, saga, outbox, contract testing, circuit breakers, distributed tracing, domain-driven design bounded contexts, modular monolith first). Say where you are unsure or where evidence is mostly anecdotal.

children.title: Write the final answer
children.instructions: Write the final deliverable: lead with a one- or two-sentence overall answer (including when splitting may not be worth it). Then present the risks as a compact table or list with columns/fields: Risk, What goes wrong, Mitigation. Keep it plain and concise, ordered from most to least significant, and end with a short note on the most common mitigation theme (e.g. incremental migration and strong observability).
